title: Grade 3 Science — Wed, Jun 18
description: Water — Day 3 of 5: States of water (solid, liquid, gas)
subject: science

questions.question: Water exists in ___ states in nature.
questions.explanation: Water exists in three states: solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapour/steam).

questions.question: Ice is water in its ___ state.
questions.explanation: Ice is the solid form of water. Water freezes (turns to ice) at 0°C.

questions.question: Water vapour (steam) is water in its ___ state.
questions.explanation: Water vapour is the gaseous form of water. Water turns to vapour (boils) at 100°C and slowly evaporates even at lower temperatures.

questions.question: When ice melts, it changes from solid to ___.
questions.explanation: Ice melts and becomes liquid water. This happens when temperature rises above 0°C.

questions.question: The process of liquid water turning into water vapour is called:
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process of liquid water turning into water vapour (gas). It happens on the surface of water, even at room temperature.

questions.question: At what temperature does water freeze (turn to ice)?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0°C (the freezing point). Below 0°C, liquid water turns to ice.

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil (turn to steam quickly)?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C (at sea level). At this temperature, liquid water rapidly turns to water vapour/steam.

questions.question: When water vapour in the air cools, it turns back to liquid. This is called:
questions.explanation: Condensation is when water vapour cools and turns back to liquid water. This is how droplets form on a cold glass or how clouds form.

questions.question: Dew drops on grass in the morning are formed by:
options: Condensation of water vapour on cool surfaces
questions.explanation: At night, grass cools down. Water vapour in the air condenses (turns to liquid) on the cool grass blades, forming dew drops.

questions.question: Clouds are made of:
options: Tiny water droplets and/or ice crystals
questions.explanation: Clouds are formed when water vapour rises, cools, and condenses into tiny water droplets or ice crystals that float in the air.

questions.question: When you take a bottle of cold water out of the fridge, water droplets form on the outside. Why?
options: The cold bottle cools the air around it → water vapour condenses
The bottle absorbs water from the air
questions.explanation: The cold bottle chills the air touching it. Water vapour in that air cools below condensation point and turns back to liquid on the bottle's surface.

questions.question: Wet clothes on a clothesline dry because:
options: The wind blows the water away
Water evaporates from the clothes into the air
questions.explanation: Heat and wind cause water to evaporate from wet clothes. The water molecules escape as water vapour into the air, leaving the clothes dry.

questions.question: Match: solid → liquid is ___, liquid → gas is ___, gas → liquid is ___.
questions.explanation: Solid → liquid = melting; liquid → gas = evaporation; gas → liquid = condensation.

questions.question: Snow is made of:
questions.explanation: Snow is made of tiny ice crystals — water frozen at very low temperatures in clouds. Each snowflake is a unique ice crystal.

questions.question: A teapot of water is heated. First you see steam; then if the steam touches a cold lid, droplets form. This shows:
questions.explanation: Boiling water → steam (evaporation). Steam hitting the cold lid → droplets (condensation). Both changes of state happen in sequence.
